title: Smooth section pairs and their canonical DNC and base-change arrows
statement: For a scheme $B$ [def-pc-scheme] and $d\in\mathbf N$, define a smooth section pair $X=(V,g,s)$ to consist of a scheme $V$, a separated quasi-compact map $g:V\to B$ smooth of pure relative dimension $d$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], a closed immersion $s:B\hookrightarrow V$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], and the equation $g\circ s=1_B$. For any $b:B'\to B$ and pairs $X',X$, define a base-change square to consist of $a:V'\to V$ for which the square with $g',g,b$ is Cartesian [def-pc-fibre-product] and $a\circ s'=s\circ b$. No flatness is required. Use the finite purity datum $P$ [def-pur-conventions], its coefficient ring $A$, and a finite-type $k$-structure $a_B$ on $B$. Define the invariant of $X$ to be the actual pro-etale section invariant $C(g,s)=Ls^*\omega_g$ [def-pur-section-invariant], with its canonical ordinary-etale presentation [def-pur-finite-section-comparison]. Define the normal pair by the actual associated-graded normal cone of $s$, its retraction-defined projection and its zero section [def-pur-normal-bundle] [lem-pur-dnc-section-geometry]. When $a_B$ is also separated, define $\delta_X:C(g,s)\simeq C(\pi_N,z)$ by the unique coordinate-normalized DNC invariance isomorphism of [thm-pur-dnc-invariance]. For finite-type structures on $B,B'$ and a base-change square as above, define $c_X:b^*C(g,s)\simeq C(g',s')$ by the counit-normalized exceptional section exchange [def-pur-co-smoothness], transported by the canonical finite section and pullback site-comparison arrows [def-pur-section-pullback-site-comparisons]. This definition specifies these pairs, objects and canonical arrows, and asserts no coherence equation among them.
